itinerary.summary: Amer Fort early, Jal Mahal on the way back, and the city lights from Nahargarh.

place.name: Amer Fort
place.description: A honey-coloured fort-palace above Maota Lake, with the mirror-work Sheesh Mahal and courtyards that light up in the early sun. Arriving at 8 means you see it before the tour buses.

morning.tip: Walk or take a jeep up; skip the elephant rides. The composite ticket also covers Nahargarh, Albert Hall and Jantar Mantar.

place.name: Jal Mahal and lunch on Amer Road
place.description: A photo stop at the palace that seems to float on Man Sagar Lake, then lunch nearby on dal baati churma, Rajasthan's signature baked wheat balls with lentils.

afternoon.tip: The palace itself is closed to visitors; the promenade is the view.

place.name: Nahargarh Fort sunset
place.description: The ridge-top fort looks straight down on the whole city. Stay for sunset as Jaipur's lights come on, then eat at the fort's terrace café.

evening.tip: Book a cab both ways; the road up is steep and winding.

itinerary.summary: The royal city centre, bazaars and a rooftop view of Hawa Mahal.

place.name: City Palace and Jantar Mantar
place.description: The royal family still lives in part of the City Palace; the museum rooms and the four seasonal gates of Pritam Niwas Chowk are open to visitors. Next door, Jantar Mantar's 18th-century instruments include the world's largest stone sundial.

morning.tip: Hire a licensed guide at Jantar Mantar; the instruments make much more sense explained.

place.name: Johari and Bapu Bazaar
place.description: Block-printed textiles, mojari slippers and silver along the pink arcades. Stop at Lassiwala on MI Road for a clay cup of thick lassi and at Rawat Mishthan Bhandar for pyaaz kachori.

afternoon.tip: Prices are open to bargaining; start at around half of the first quote.

place.name: Hawa Mahal and a rooftop dinner
place.description: See the 953-window 'Palace of Winds' from the front, then climb to one of the cafés opposite for a rooftop dinner looking straight at its façade.

evening.tip: The best view is from the cafés across the road, not from inside the palace.

stays.name: Samode Haveli
stays.why: A 19th-century haveli with painted rooms and a pool, walkable to the old city.

stays.name: Alsisar Haveli
stays.why: Rajput architecture and courtyards at a mid-range price.

stays.name: Zostel Jaipur
stays.why: Social, central and budget-friendly, with private rooms too.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Hindi and Rajasthani; English widely understood
essentials.weather: Oct-Mar is pleasant (8-28°C); Apr-Jun is fierce heat above 40°C.
essentials.gettingAround: Uber, Ola and autos are cheap; agree the auto fare first.
essentials.phrase: Khamma ghani: a warm Rajasthani hello

packing: Scarf for sun and temple visits

summary.overview: A tight, well-paced 48 hours in the Pink City: the hill fort of Amer at opening time, the City Palace and Jantar Mantar, old-city bazaars, and a rooftop dinner facing Hawa Mahal.
highlights: Lassi and kachori in the old city
